sentences.text: Shri Abhay Saraswat - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Bhaskar Agrawal - Public Prosecutor for the respon
Heard on I.A No.9887/2025 , which is first application under Section 430 of BNSS for grant of suspension of sentence filed on behalf of appellant Rajkumar.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 363, 366, 376(3), 506(II) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I for 5 years, 5 years, life imprisonment, 1 year, life imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/-, Rs.1000/-, Rs.2000/-, Rs.500/-, Rs.2000/- with default stipulation.
Counsel for the appellant submits that the appeal is of the year 2024 and final hearing of the same may take time.
He further argues that as per the prosecution case, the prosecutrix was abducted and subjected to sexual exploitation which is incorrect.
The prosecutrix has remained with the appellant for about 12 days without raising any alarm.
The source of recording the age of the prosecutrix in the scholar register has not been proved.

In the case of Tijubai @ Omvati Bai and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2025(1) MPLJ (Cri.)75, it has been held that if the prosecution does not prove the source of date of birth recorded in scholar register and the same is recorded on the guess, the same cannot be the basis for conviction.

entities.text: Tijubai @ Omvati Bai and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2025(1) MPLJ (Cri.)75,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The age of the appellant at the time of incident was 21 years.
Counsel for the State supports the order of conviction and sentence.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the prosecution has failed to prove the source of recording the age of prosecutrix in the scholar register, the judgment passed in the case of Tijubai (supra) and the fact that the age of the appellant was 21 years at the time of incident, we are of the considered opinion that the appellant is entitled for grant of suspension of sentence.
Accordingly, I.A No.9887/2025 is allowed.

The jail sentence of appellant Rajkumar is suspended Rajkumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17239230/
1 upon his depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees fifty thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 22.4.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Registry.
